title: Discharge clean: sequence from assessment to remaking the bed
audience: Cleaning staff in South Australian public healthcare facilities who clean patient rooms after discharge
learningOutcomes: Perform the steps of a discharge clean in the right sequence
Remove and bag used linen without spreading contamination
Check the sharps container and waste before leaving the room

instruction.heading: Before you touch anything
instruction.body: A discharge clean takes place after the patient has left and before the following patient enters. First check whether a transmission-based precaution applied to the patient who left. Then walk the room and note what must be replaced: toilet tissue, hand towels, soap, hand rub, gloves and the sharps container. Make this list before you start on the bed, so nothing is missed at the end.

instruction.heading: Working order inside the room
instruction.body: Work from least soiled to most soiled and starting from the highest surfaces down. Begin by stripping the bed and bagging the linen where it lies, rolling sheets carefully to limit the spread of aerosols. Put on fresh gloves once the linen is out of the way. Then clean the door, its handle and touched areas, walls only where they look dirty, switches, thermostats and wall-mounted items. Move on to furnishings and flat surfaces, then equipment such as drip stands, the locker, the bed frame and mattress. Clean the bathroom and the floors near the end. Use a fresh cloth for each bed space, and never dip a used cloth back into the clean solution.

instruction.heading: Finishing and leaving
instruction.body: Before you leave, check the sharps container and replace it once it reaches the fill point in the standard. Put in a new linen bag, then close waste bags without pressing down on them with your hands. Take off your gloves, clean your hands with hand rub unless they look dirty, and leave the room without gloves on. Remake the bed, restock the room, and return the equipment you moved to its storage area. The standard sets the fill point for sharps containers at three-quarters full. The Irish manual uses a different fraction; in SA the standard governs.

procedure: Check whether a transmission-based precaution applied to the patient who left.
Walk the room and list what must be replaced.
Assemble fresh solution made to the label and enough clean cloths.
Perform hand hygiene then glove up.
Strip the bed and bag the linen at the point of use; remove gloves, then clean hands.
Put on fresh gloves, then clean the room from least soiled to most soiled and top to bottom, using a fresh cloth for each bed space.
Clean the bathroom and floors, then review the checklist and sign.
Check the sharps container, bag the waste and remove the linen bag.
Remove gloves, clean hands, remake the bed, restock and return equipment.

workedExamples.situation: Bed 2 in a four-bed bay held a patient on contact precautions who was discharged at 10:00. The next admission is booked for 11:30.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which method applies, and what must be prepared before the first cloth goes near a surface?
workedExamples.reasoning: The clean is transmission-based, so the method is detergent and disinfectant. Before cleaning, make fresh solution to the label, collect clean cloths for the bed space, check the sharps container, and choose the PPE the precaution calls for. Gowns or masks are added only where the precaution or the risk assessment requires them.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves for each stage of the task
Clean cloths, one per bed space
Fresh cleaning solution made to the label
Clinical waste bags plus linen bags

commonErrors.error: Cleaning the bathroom before the bed is stripped
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the room order: linen first, then high to low and clean to dirty.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the room with gloves still on
commonErrors.prevention: Remove gloves, clean hands, then leave.

commonErrors.error: Filling a sharps container past its fill point
commonErrors.prevention: Check the fill mark before starting and again before leaving.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Handle used linen as if it is contaminated. Bag it at the point of use and never place it on the ground.
Pick up sharps with tongs or a mechanical tool, do not recap used needles, and tell your supervisor about every sharps incident.

Sharps container fill point: the SA standard (2014, updated 2017) uses three-quarters full. The Irish HSE manual gives a different fill point, which is not used here. In SA follow the standard and local policy. The figure is historical; confirm current policy.

qualityStandard: The learner performs the steps in the right sequence in a walkthrough
The learner checks the sharps container and waste before leaving
The learner removes gloves and cleans hands before leaving the room
documentationEvidence: Completed discharge clean checklist signed by the cleaner
Record of any sharps or linen incident reported to the supervisor
summary: Walk the room first and list what must be replaced
Linen comes out first and is bagged at the point of use
Check the sharps container and leave the room without gloves on

knowledgeChecks.question: When should the sharps container be checked during a discharge clean?
options: Only at the end of the week

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is used linen bagged where it is used?
options: So the bed looks neat for the next patient and the staff like it
To keep contaminated linen off the floor and away from staff clothing
Because laundry is charged by the bag and the bags are cheap

knowledgeChecks.question: Which order best describes a discharge clean in a ward room?
options: Bathroom first, then bed, then doors and the floors are cleaned in the middle of the job
Linen and bed area first, then doors and touched areas, with floors and the bathroom near the end
Floors first so the room dries sooner and the bed is left until the very end of the clean
